title: Financing the Buyer: From Conversation to Clear to Close
originality: All items original to LicensePath. Modeled on the DRE exam blueprint and style only; no actual exam items reproduced.

questions.stem: Which milestone most strongly indicates that lender conditions have been completed and the loan is ready for closing steps?
options: Prequalification
Preapproval
Clear to close
A buyer's verbal statement
rationales: A prequalification is an early estimate and is not a completed loan review.
A preapproval can still contain borrower and property conditions.
Correct. A clear to close follows satisfaction of required underwriting conditions, although final process steps still remain.
A buyer cannot independently determine that a lender has cleared a file.

questions.stem: A $640,000 loan on an $800,000 purchase price has an LTV of:
rationales: Twenty percent is the down-payment percentage in this example, not the LTV.
Dividing 640,000 by one million would produce 64%, but one million is not the value here.
An LTV above 100% would mean the loan exceeds the stated value.

questions.stem: A buyer asks the agent whether a particular rate is the best loan for them. The agent should first:
options: Promise the rate is excellent because the lender is preferred
Explain that the lender should compare terms and costs with the buyer
Tell the buyer to waive the loan contingency
Choose the loan product based on the listing agent's preference
rationales: An agent should not make an unsupported loan recommendation or guarantee.
Correct. The agent may help the buyer frame questions, but the lender must explain product terms and the buyer makes the financing decision.
A contingency decision should follow informed analysis, not replace it.
The listing side does not choose the buyer's financing.

questions.stem: A home is under contract for $900,000. The appraisal is $875,000 and the lender will lend 80% of appraised value. What is the maximum stated loan amount?
rationales: $720,000 is 80% of the contract price, not the lower appraised value.
The appraisal is not itself the loan amount.
The contract price is not the lender's 80% maximum in this fact pattern.

questions.stem: Which buyer action should prompt an immediate conversation with the lender before closing?
options: Opening a new auto loan
Reviewing the preliminary report
Scheduling a final walk-through
Asking escrow for signing times
rationales: Correct. New debt can affect credit and debt-to-income underwriting; the lender should assess it before the buyer acts.
Reviewing title is important but does not itself change borrower qualification.
A final walk-through is a normal transaction activity.
Signing logistics do not normally affect loan qualification.

questions.stem: A lender tells an agent that underwriting needs another document. The most appropriate update to the listing side is:
options: The buyer will certainly close on time
The lender needs an additional document and an updated status will follow by a stated time
The buyer's income and account balances in detail
Nothing; status updates are never appropriate
rationales: No one should promise an outcome before the lender confirms it.
Correct. This is factual, protects private information, and gives the other side a reliable next update.
Detailed financial information is private and unnecessary for transaction coordination.
Appropriate milestone communication can prevent avoidable escalation.

questions.stem: A seller credit is best described as:
options: Cash the buyer may always receive after closing
A contribution that can apply only as permitted by the contract and loan program
A replacement for buyer qualification
A guarantee that an appraisal will meet contract price
rationales: Unused credit does not automatically become cash to the buyer.
Correct. Allowable use and limits depend on the contract and loan program, which the lender confirms.
A credit does not replace income, assets, credit, or underwriting.
An appraisal is independent of a seller-credit request.

questions.stem: Which form is intended to help a borrower understand estimated loan terms and costs after application in a covered consumer mortgage transaction?
options: Transfer Disclosure Statement
Loan Estimate
Preliminary report
Grant deed
rationales: A TDS concerns property condition disclosures, not loan terms.
Correct. The Loan Estimate summarizes estimated loan terms and costs.
A preliminary report identifies title matters rather than lender pricing.
A grant deed transfers a real-property interest.

questions.stem: A buyer is purchasing a condominium. Which financing issue should the agent raise early with the lender?
options: Whether project review or property eligibility requirements apply
Whether the buyer should ignore HOA documents
Whether the appraiser can be pressured to support value
Whether title is unnecessary because the buyer has a loan
rationales: Correct. Condominium projects can involve lender review and should be discussed before a deadline creates pressure.
HOA documents can be material to both buyer due diligence and lender review.
Appraiser independence is important; pressure is improper.
Title review remains important in financed transactions.

questions.stem: An email says escrow's wiring instructions have changed and asks the buyer to send funds immediately. The safest response is to:
options: Use the new instructions because the email looks professional
Reply to the email asking for confirmation
Verify instructions through a known independently confirmed escrow phone number
Send half the funds first
rationales: Email appearance is not reliable protection against wire fraud.
Replying can still communicate with a compromised account.
Correct. Independently verifying through a known phone number is the appropriate fraud-control step.
Sending a partial wire still risks loss and does not verify instructions.

questions.stem: A buyer plans to borrow $500,000 on a $625,000 purchase. Before closing costs, the planned down payment is:
rationales: $100,000 would leave a $525,000 loan.
$500,000 is the planned loan amount.
$625,000 is the full purchase price.

questions.stem: Which statement about a preapproval is most accurate?
options: It always means all borrower and property conditions have been satisfied
It has the identical scope at every lender
It can reduce uncertainty but should be read for remaining conditions and verification
It permits the agent to guarantee closing
rationales: Property, income, asset, appraisal, and other conditions may remain.
Lenders do not necessarily use the label for the same review depth.
Correct. Ask what was verified, what remains, and whether property type or timing conditions apply.
Only the lender can determine loan approval; an agent cannot guarantee closing.

questions.stem: Which referral practice is most consistent with fair and consumer-focused financing service?
options: Directing buyers to a lender based on a protected characteristic
Giving every buyer the same neutral referral criteria and preserving lender choice
Requiring use of the brokerage's preferred lender
Withholding lender options until after offer acceptance
rationales: Protected characteristics are not a lawful basis for financing referrals.
Correct. Neutral criteria, consistent service, and buyer choice reduce discrimination and conflict risk.
A preferred lender list is not a mandate.
Buyers benefit from understanding financing options before they write an offer.

questions.stem: Which item is not necessarily included in a simple PITI estimate?
options: Principal
Interest
Homeowners-association dues
Property taxes
rationales: The P in PITI includes principal.
The I in PITI includes interest.
Correct. HOA dues may be a real housing cost, but they are not one of the four PITI components.
The T in PITI includes property taxes.

questions.stem: A low appraisal occurs while the buyer's appraisal contingency remains in effect. Which is the best agent action?
options: Tell the buyer the seller must reduce price
Review the contract, confirm lender options, and explain the buyer's available transaction paths
Assure the seller that the appraisal can be changed by request
Ignore the appraisal until closing
rationales: The seller's response depends on negotiation and contract terms; it is not automatic.
Correct. Contract language, lender options, buyer funds, and timing determine the practical paths.
An appraisal reconsideration has a lender process and is not guaranteed.
Ignoring the issue can cause a preventable closing failure.

questions.stem: Why should insurance be investigated early for a property in a higher-risk fire area?
options: Insurance is unrelated to financing
Availability and cost can affect closing and buyer qualification
The seller's agent can bind the buyer's policy
It removes the need for a home inspection
rationales: Lenders commonly require acceptable insurance as a closing condition.
Correct. Insurance availability, terms, and cost can affect whether and how the buyer closes.
An agent generally cannot bind an insurance policy for a buyer.
Insurance and inspections serve different purposes.

questions.stem: The Closing Disclosure is designed primarily to show:
options: The seller's marketing plan
Final loan terms and costs
The property's legal description only
The buyer's inspection findings
rationales: Marketing is unrelated to mortgage disclosures.
Correct. The Closing Disclosure presents final loan terms and costs for covered transactions.
A legal description may appear in other transaction documents but is not the form's primary purpose.
Inspection findings are not the purpose of a Closing Disclosure.

questions.stem: A buyer makes a large cash deposit shortly before underwriting. The agent should advise the buyer to:
options: Hide the deposit by moving it again
Promptly ask the lender what source documentation is needed
Cancel the transaction immediately
Tell the seller all details of the deposit
rationales: Moving or hiding funds can worsen underwriting and fraud concerns.
Correct. The lender can explain documentation requirements; prompt, accurate response protects the timeline.
The issue may be resolvable with documentation and does not automatically require cancellation.
The buyer's financial detail is private and generally unnecessary for the seller.
